ATAC-seq and RNA-seq use independent samples. GEO GSE82015 lists four wild-type ATAC replicates at E0/E1/E4 and two sh-cFos E1 ATAC replicates; other AAV ATAC groups and RNA groups have three. GSE86367 lists three E24 ATAC and three RNA samples. Replicate labels do not independently verify animal identity or sample independence.

c-Fos knockdown uses one shRNA and overexpression uses AAV2/9 one week before assay. No reviewed rescue with a second sequence excludes all off-target effects. External KCl-neuron ChIP-seq annotations are not matched in vivo c-Fos occupancy measurements.

A 1/4/24-hour comparison across sacrificed cohorts does not demonstrate persistence in the same cell, lifelong memory, inheritance or a universal minimal assembly. RNA abundance is distinct from transcription rate, protein output and behavioral function.

Figure 6c has a 144/114 gene-count conflict. Figure 7c caption says E0/E4/E24, while plot and experimental text specify E0/E1/E4. Supplementary Tables 4-5 contain conflicting headers, nonfinite values or spreadsheet errors. No global quantitative model is calibrated from these data.

The main Methods report no sample-size predetermination, randomization or blinding. Some qPCR primer labels/sequences conflict. Published findings, metadata inspection and source-cell counts are not independent biological replication or sequencing-pipeline reproduction.

Approximately three-month-old male Arc-CreERT2/R26R-eYFP mice on a C57BL/6J background. Training includes a tone paired with footshock in a context; the changed-context comparison alters several environmental cues. It is not a context-only learning protocol or an isolated chromatin intervention.

Basal denotes NeuN+/eYFP- nuclei collected after training, not naive home-cage animals. Early denotes NeuN+/eYFP+ at 1.5-2 hours, Late the tagged population at five days without recall, and Reactivated NeuN+/eYFP+/Arc+ after re-exposure in a different cohort. Marker selection, reporter maturation and a roughly 12-hour labeling window limit cell identity and temporal specificity.

Whole-hippocampus molecular samples pool nuclei across animals and neuronal subtypes. ATAC Methods specify 10,000 nuclei from 8-10 mice per replicate. Table 13 lists three Basal and four Late libraries, while the reporting summary excludes one Basal from 13 and Figure 2a states n=3 per group. The included-library mapping remains unresolved. A library, genomic locus, slice or punctum is not an independent animal. Destructive cohorts are not single-cell longitudinal measurements.

Figure 1f counts are labeled cells per DG slice; the caption refers to hippocampus. Its five versus six mice each contribute six sections, while tests report df=59/57. Extended Data 1e gives n=15 with df=14 without a clear per-group denominator; 1c has n=30 with df=16. Animal-level effects and confidence intervals require source measurements and sample reconciliation.

Hi-C Methods describe two libraries per Basal, Early and Late population, but the reporting summary excludes one Early library. Methods say two animals per sample, whereas reporting specifies four to five. Promoter-capture Hi-C covers four populations and selected promoters. Contact frequencies and inferred A/B compartments are not unique three-dimensional coordinates. Figure 3 specifies a 500-kb Juicer representation, while Methods and software use 50-kb HOMER compartment PCA; their mapping needs explicit reconstruction.

ATAC Figure 2a labels log2 fold-change thresholds, while its caption, Methods and software say fold changes >1.5. RNA Table 8 has undocumented sign reorientation and a near-threshold extra row. The RNA Methods cite an edgeR reference for DESeq2 and the software omits the RNA export code. No sequence analysis, signed gene-specific pathway or edge weight is calibrated.

eIF4E and GRIA1 puncta measure protein immunoreactivity, not translation rate, receptor current or synaptic efficacy. The Results/caption call the measured shaft dendritic, but Figure 5f labels an axon and Methods describe axon surfaces; exact compartment identity and distance units require clarification. Sections and neurites are nested within mice.

Reported group randomization and selected blinded quantification do not resolve all sampling issues. Sequencing sample sizes used observed variability and group differences; ATAC/Hi-C quality exclusions and a plotted ATAC outlier exclusion were not pre-established. Normality was assumed without formal testing. Null tests are not equivalence tests. Separate molecular profiles and behavioral outcomes do not establish a chromatin-to-memory mediation chain or lifelong persistence.

Accessibility and contact-frequency profiles are not direct chromatin-density, unique three-dimensional packing, mechanical force or molecular remodeling trajectories. RNA abundance is not a transcription rate or a direct replication/repair-permissibility measurement.

Separate profiles and populations do not establish that packing causes the expression differences. c-Fos perturbation has multiple possible routes; matching ATAC/RNA effects does not uniquely identify accessibility as their mediator.

Population-level region overlap through sampled windows is not an inherited state, a persistent same-cell trajectory, a universal physical sequence-to-functional-resource transformation or complete spatial control of genomic function.

Epigenetic regulation, nucleic-acid copying, hydrogen bonding and signal pathways are separate scopes. A named chromatin role does not make them necessary causal ancestors or substitute for a matched packaging intervention.

Thalamic visual transfer is reconstructed through paired-spike retinal efficacy and separate corticogeniculate perturbation results. These observations distinguish retinal transmission from cortical feedback and exclude one universal positive-gain sign. Identical demographic/pathology fields occur for some different IDs; this does not prove duplicate donors. The donor/sample manifest and independence remain unresolved.

Table 8 filter_counts contains 153530 retained nuclei across 39 samples. The paper reports 355997 sequenced nuclei. These are different processing stages, not an established count contradiction; a complete retained/excluded-nucleus manifest has not been reconstructed.

The abundance analysis uses per-sample counts and library-size normalization, not absolute whole-hippocampus numbers or neuron birth rates. Published log-fold changes and adjusted P values are retained as reported comparisons; edgeR analysis and sequencing data have not been rerun.

SuperAgers come from Northwestern, while the other groups come from the University of Washington. Tissue source, individual variability and clinical selection can confound group comparisons. The Methods and main text differ in their reference age wording for SuperAger memory criteria; a uniform clinical manifest is required.

Age associations use cross-sectional, model-derived rates: reported neuronal r=-0.31, P=0.03 and nonneuronal r=-0.35, P=0.04. They do not trace the same people over time or identify an age intervention. The sex comparison P=0.41 does not establish equivalence. The DCX overlay uses an external Knoth cohort, not birthdating of the same cells.

The accepted supplement prints a heuristic labeled AIC, p + log2(SSE), and requires a halving of SSE per added parameter. Applying that printed rule to rounded Table S2 gives 0.31 > 0.51/2, so its nonneuronal 2POP preference does not follow from that rule. Table S3 has 0.17 < 0.49/2 for neurons. This arithmetic checks reporting consistency only; final supplementary methods, likelihood and code remain unverified.

The source says subjects born around 1955-1965 discriminate 2POP from homogeneous age-dependent alternatives; without them the scenarios could not be distinguished. MCMC explores bounded parameter sets, and fitting several scenarios does not prove a unique biological mechanism. Full numerical replay and out-of-sample discrimination have not been performed.

The fitting procedure assumes a one-year food lag and development beginning six months before birth. Its weighted SSE squares weights of 1 or 2 assigned around a 10-microgram carbon boundary. Table S1 has both estimated DNA carbon mass and reactor-measured mass, including ND entries. The exact mass choice, boundary treatment and missing-value policy require executable code before reproducing the fit.

The supplement explicitly does not explore population feedback: birth and death rates do not depend on the population state. Constant population size in replacement scenarios is imposed by their birth boundary, not observed emergence of a stabilizing rule. Population turnover does not identify one-for-one functional replacement, circuit topology or a universal minimal assembly.

The SA immature-cell comparison is significant against HA and AD, but not against YA or PCI at the table adjusted-P threshold of 0.05. These distinct contrasts neither prove no difference nor establish that generating neurons preserves memory.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

The paper explicitly leaves functional significance untested. No electrical recording, identified synaptic output, behavioral mediation or selective birth-cell perturbation establishes functional integration in these human samples. Findings in mouse integration experiments cannot supply those missing human measurements.

Whole hippocampi were analyzed; the investigators could not separately radiocarbon-date hippocampal subdivisions. Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

QED_L removes spatial photon zero modes on every time slice. QED_TL removes only the four-momentum zero mode and has an ill-defined T-to-infinity limit at fixed L for the conventional charged-particle mass extraction. This is a regulator distinction, not two experimental forces.

At order alpha, the leading mass correction is -q^2*alpha*kappa/(2*L)*(1+2/(m*L)), with kappa approximately 2.837297 in units hbar=c=1. Universality through 1/L^2 assumes the photon is the only massless asymptotic state and the charged particle is stable and nondegenerate with states sharing its quantum numbers.

Terms of order 1/L^3 can depend on internal structure and spin; a point-fermion coefficient cannot be imposed on every hadron. Vanishing leading q^2 terms for a neutral particle do not prove absence of all finite-volume effects.

In the full QCD+QED theory the paper's continuum prescription retains an extremely small nonzero cutoff because of QED triviality. Its practical extrapolation does not establish a nonperturbative interacting QED limit at exactly zero lattice spacing.

At the stated precision the recoil prescription is E_B approximately E_gamma + E_gamma^2/(2*m_d*c^2), so the energy-equivalent wavelength is shorter than the photon wavelength. It is not a second detected photon.

The recoil mass is the deuteron nuclear mass, not a deuterium atomic mass or the Kapton molecular mass. Thermal capture and the stated prompt-emission conditions limit this approximation; it is not an exact arbitrary-kinematics formula.

The paper reports a 5e-10 relative uncertainty contribution from recoil constants, negligible at its measurement precision. This does not make recoil itself negligible or set omitted kinematic effects identically to zero.

The 1999 inverse-meter conversions are 1.331025045(11)e-15 u and 1.239841870(54)e-6 eV per inverse meter. The first is a mass-equivalent conversion h/(m_u*c), the second is hc/e; energy and mass units are not interchangeable without c^2.

The conversions depend on the paper's electron relative mass, fine-structure constant, Rydberg constant and other adopted constants. Their uncertainties are different; changing to modern SI constants is a new calculation, not a silent correction of the published result.

The later author report uses d220(ILL2.5)=1.920155822(96)e-10 m, retaining a 5e-8 relative uncertainty after enlarging the underlying adjustment uncertainty. Its deuterium row reuses Kessler data and is not a new capture experiment.

The earlier wavelength and mass cannot be combined with a later crystal spacing or conversion constant while retaining their old central values. Recalculation is required; this review does not replay the underlying lattice adjustment.

For the selected ambient-water structure analysis, the oxygen-oxygen pair-distribution function g_OO(r) describes a radial spatial correlation of oxygen positions. A distance-shell coordination is an integral of 4*pi*rho_O*r^2*g_OO(r) over stated radial bounds. It is distinct from a unique angular hydrogen-bond network, cluster identity or time correlation. In the selected dynamics model, C_n(t)=average P_n[u_OH(0) dot u_OH(t)] characterizes orientational decorrelation, while a completed hydrogen-bond partner exchange uses its own state definition and endpoint conditions. Static pair structure, orientational relaxation, exchange waiting time, angular-event duration and molecular persistence are different quantities.

The infinitely long cylindrical-electrode approximation gives a relative cyclotron correction approximately m/(4*pi*epsilon0*B0^2*rho0^3). Real gaps, electrode shape, displacements and axial fields require a scoped geometry calculation.
